sources.entry: Introduction to SVE - Where Arm explains vector-length-agnostic loops and predication, the model that removes remainder loops entirely.

summary.title: Introduction to SVE
summary.one_liner: Arm's introduction to the Scalable Vector Extension (SVE), covering its concepts, main features, application domains, and how it compares to Neon.
keywords: sve vector length power of two
takeaways: SVE is Arm's scalable vector extension, introduced in this guide with its main concepts and features.
The guide describes the application domains where SVE is used.
It compares SVE with Neon, Arm's existing SIMD extension.
Per the revision history, SVE vector length is restricted to a power of two (issue 0101-01, February 2025).

The page's listing notes that vector-length-agnostic loops and predication can remove remainder loops; the page text provided here contains only front matter and legal notices, so those details are not confirmed from this text.
summary.summary: This is the Arm support documentation titled "Introduction to SVE" (version 1.1). The text provided is mostly front matter: release history, legal disclaimers, confidentiality status, and feedback instructions. The page's meta description says it covers the concept and main features of SVE, its application domains, and how SVE compares to Neon. The body sections on those topics were not included in the supplied page text, so technical details are not confirmed here beyond the listing's note about vector-length-agnostic loops and predication.
